meta_description: The question is not whether to fine-tune but who owns the resulting model risk.

blocks.x: The question is not whether to fine-tune but who owns the resulting model risk.

Fine-tuning is a governance decision, not a modeling one is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. The evidence is consistent across industries — the constraint is rarely technology; it is whether the operating model takes this seriously from sprint one.

items: Curated corpora beat corpus size; licensing and PII posture decide auditability.
LoRA/QLoRA economics make iteration weekly: if the registry and eval gates exist.
EU AI Act technical documentation is cheapest when generated during training, not after.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: What is the classical baseline every proposed capability must beat, measured on identical data?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
Show us a negative result you documented: the discipline is the product.

blocks.x: The failure mode is predictable: enthusiasm funds the demo, budget cycles gate the industrialization, and by the time the governance conversation starts, shadow usage has already created the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

items: Pre-agreed criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
Named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
Replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Domain evals typically gain +15-25 points over frontier prompting after disciplined adaptation.
